item.title: This Week in Spring - August 11th, 2026
item.dc:creator: joshlong
item.content:encoded:
Hi, Spring fans! Welcome back to another lively edition of This Week in Spring! So much is always happening in the Spring world, and that¡¯s part of what makes it so fun to follow. One of my favorite things is how much the community contributes and how great it is to connect with everyone. In early September, I¡¯ll be in Oslo, Norway, for the JavaZone conference, and then in Amsterdam for the IntelliJ IDEA conference. But before we get there, it¡¯s been a busy and exciting week, so let¡¯s jump in.

  • I did a video looking at the amazing JobRunr distributed job scheduling and execution engine
  • In last week's installment of A Bootiful Podcast, I was thrilled to chat with Tanzu's very own Gregory Green about RabbitMQ, Valkey, GemFire, Data Flow, and so much more
  • A nice video on deploying Spring AI-powered agents to AgentCore in no time at all
  • Speaking of, Spring AI AgentCore 2.1.0 is out!
  • Another amazing post from Craig Walls on making Spring AI-powered agents conversation-aware.
  • I loved this interview on the Marco Show with Spring Framework, Spring AOT, Kotlin, and Spring AI contributor and guru Sebastien Deleuze
  • A very interesting discussion on the implications (good and sometimes surprising) of introducing virtual threads to a Java 24 project
  • Speaking of AI (more?), I'm pleased that Broadcom, where I and most of the Spring team work, is now part of the Open Secure AI Alliance
  • This video is now a month old, but I promise you, you'll probably learn something, so check it out: From Brackets to Beans to Boot
  • Amazon's James Ward has a great idea on how to dramatically improve token consumption, and he shows DaShaun Carter and me how with a Spring AI-based implementation in this amazing livestream

item.title: A Bootiful Podcast: Data guru Gregory Green on RabbitMQ, Valkey, Gemfire, Data Flow, and more
item.dc:creator: joshlong
item.content:encoded: Hi, Spring and data fans! Want a faster, smarter data stack? Tune into this episode with Gregory Green for a deep dive into GemFire, RabbitMQ Streams, Dataflow, and more. We cover real-time event processing, active-active consistency, full-text search, vector search, and how to build resilient, scalable systems with less complexity. Don¡¯t miss it.

item.title: This Week in Spring - August 4th, 2026
item.dc:creator: joshlong
item.content:encoded:
Hi, Spring fans! Welcome to another installment of This Week in Spring! It's the 4th of August! We're already in month eight of this year! Great Scott!

  • This is an interesting project to help ensure idempotency keys for Spring Boot requests
  • A very interesting post on The New Stack titled, When vendor-supplied support matters: [How AI is changing the open source security equation], which features commentary from our very own Ryan Morgan](https://thenewstack.io/ai-open-source-security/)
  • Have you heard about agentic loops? Check out this nice explainer on what it is and why it matters
  • I loved this explainer on RabbitMQ Streams! by Gregory Green
  • I really liked this talk by Neo4j founder Emil Eifrem on AI ontologies
  • I was very happy to be interviewed on the Marco Behler JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA team a few weeks ago
  • Last week I was thrilled to sit down and chat with Spring Boot cofounder Phil Webb about the latest and greatest!
  • I like this post looking at dynamic configuration with Spring Cloud
  • Wow! Look at this! A whole workshop-style thing looking at microservices with Spring Cloud
  • Wanna integrate DynamoDB into your Spring Boot application? Baeldung's got a nice post

item.title: A Bootiful Podcast: Spring Boot founder and lead Phil Webb
item.dc:creator: joshlong
item.content:encoded: Hi, Spring fans! In this installment I talk to Spring Boot cofounder Phil Webb who joins the show to unpack the latest Spring Boot 4.1 release, from the long-awaited Spring gRPC support and MongoDB batch starter to security, observability, service connections, and other polished improvements.
